message.reasoning:
I'm ready to play Monopoly.

I have $209. Unmortgaging both properties would cost exactly $209, leaving me with nothing. I don't have a full monopoly yet. I'll likely end my turn.

Unmortgaging would waste cash. I'm considering trading for St. James from p4. They have a complete green monopoly and $138 cash, so they could build quickly.

p4 cannot build houses yet. One house on each green costs $200, but they only have $138.

p2 poses the real threat. They own Boardwalk and Park Place with three houses each. Rent on those spaces reaches $1400 and $1100.

p2 also has all four railroads and both utilities.

From Short Line, rolling 6 or 7 would leave me with only $9. Rolling 8, 10, or 12 would hit p1's fully built light blues or p2's St. Charles. I'm calculating the safest roll.

Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut each charge $450 to $600 with four houses. I cannot afford any of them. Rolling 8, 10, or 11 from Short Line lands me on one of those spaces. That is roughly a 28% chance of bankruptcy next turn. Reading Railroad and Income Tax are safe. I need more cash or I will die.

Selling my orange properties for cash would kill my winning path. Trading Tennessee and New York for St. James is a bad deal because I cannot complete the orange monopoly. I am weighing whether p4 might accept cash for that property.

I calculated the exact cost of buying St. James for $180 and then unmortgaging both oranges. That would leave me with only $29, which is still far short of the $209 needed to unmortgage both properties. I am now considering trading with p1.

p1 has mortgaged reds but no orange properties to trade. p2 would not pay $400 for mortgaged oranges because they lack St. James. I have little to offer p4 in exchange for St. James.

p4 will not sell St. James cheaply because it blocks my orange monopoly and I could eventually build it to threaten them. Trading with p2 is unlikely to help. I will probably just end my turn.

Selling both orange properties to p4 would crown them with a complete orange monopoly. That is a death sentence because they would then hold both greens and oranges. Selling just one property for cash would leave me with no winning path and a weak asset.

I am weighing whether to propose a trade that I do not expect to be accepted. Deception is allowed, but the engine might still ask for another post-turn action after a rejected proposal.

I will end my turn. I will not unmortgage or sell my orange properties. I will keep the $209 cash buffer. I briefly considered unmortgaging only one orange, but that would still leave me short of the $209 needed to unmortgage both.
